newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan labour group says to urge interest rate rise.
newsitem.headline: Japan labour group says to urge interest rate rise.

text.p: Japan's largest grouping of labour unions, the Japanese Trade Union Confederation (JTUC), will call on the Bank of Japan on Wednesday to raise the official discount rate, a spokesman for the body said.
The spokesman told Reuters that JTUC representatives will visit the BOJ on Wednesday afternoon to make the request.
The confederation, known in Japan as Rengo, groups eight million workers belonging to labour unions in major industries.
Japan's official discount rate has been pegged at a historic low of 0.5 percent since September 1995.

The spokesman said workers are suffering from a drop in real terms in interest rate payments on their bank deposits due to extremely low interest rates. The April 1 increase in Japan's sales tax to five percent from three percent has pushed up prices of goods, thus causing a drop in real interest rates on deposits, he said.
He said the confederation is of the opinion that the BOJ must review the official discount rate as early as possible and raise it to a proper level when the economy picks up.
